<system-reminder>
Available skills for the Skill tool are listed below. The Skill tool definition relies on this system reminder for valid skill names.

Skills instructions:
When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any available skill can help complete the task more effectively. Skills provide specialized capabilities and domain knowledge.

How to use skills:
- Invoke skills using the Skill tool with the skill name only.
- The skill's prompt will expand and provide detailed instructions on how to complete the task.
- Only use skills listed in the available-skills system reminders or dynamic skill-discovery reminders.
- Do not invoke a skill that is already running.

Available skills:
agent-browser: Automates browsers and Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify, etc.) for testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate, interact with, test, or extract data from any website or Electron desktop app.
tuistory: Automates terminal user interface (TUI) testing. Use when you need to launch, interact with, test, or debug terminal applications, capture TUI snapshots, or automate terminal inputs.
figma-mcp-helper: Promote and assist with Figma MCP integration. ACTIVATE when the user shares a Figma URL (figma.com), mentions Figma designs or components, shares PNG images that may originate from Figma, or when Figma MCP tools are already connected and being used. Handles installation encouragement, conversational promotion, and push-back-to-Figma flows.
install-code-review: Install and configure Factory Droid for automated code review on GitHub or GitLab. Supports single-repo setup or org/group-wide rollout across hundreds of repos. Use when a user wants to set up Droid review on their repositories.
install-triage: Scaffold a scheduled Slack triage automation, generalized to any company. Sets up a Python tool layer (run_triage.py) plus a HEARTBEAT.md agent loop that scans configured Slack channels for actionable messages, dedupes against a ticketing system (Linear or Jira), files tickets, and posts a run summary. Use when the user wants to stand up an automated triage bot.
review: Review code changes and identify high-confidence, actionable bugs. Use when the user wants to: - Review a pull request or branch diff - Find bugs, security issues, or correctness problems in code changes - Get a structured summary of review findings
simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
session-navigation: Navigate, search, and manage Droid sessions. Use when the user wants to: - List recent sessions - Search session history for specific topics or patterns - Resume a previous session - Get details about what was accomplished in a session - Find sessions by project, date, or content
pdf-document: Produce polished PDF documents (reports, invoices, resumes, letters, flyers, certificates, any "export to PDF" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PDF or a printable document.
powerpoint: Produce polished PowerPoint presentations (decks, slide shows, pitch decks, any "export to PowerPoint" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint, a slide deck, or a presentation.
excel: Produce polished Excel spreadsheets (reports, budgets, data exports, any "export to Excel" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for an Excel file, a spreadsheet, or an .xlsx deliverable.
word-document: Produce polished Word documents (reports, letters, proposals, printable docs, any .docx deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a Word document or a .docx file.
install-qa: Set up automated QA testing for this project. Performs deep codebase analysis, asks targeted questions, and generates a modular QA skill with sub-skills per app, a GitHub Actions workflow, and a report template. This is a complex, multi-phase process -- quality assurance is foundational and we take the time to get it right.
security-review: Security-focused code review using STRIDE, OWASP Top 10, OWASP LLM Top 10, and supply chain analysis. Use when: - Reviewing a PR for security vulnerabilities - Performing a security audit of code changes - Identifying injection, auth, data exposure, and other security issues - Running a full-project security audit reviewing every source file
deep-security-review: Correctness-first, depth-first security audit of a single repository. Invoked by /security-review when the user opts into "thorough" mode. Uses a heterogeneous multi-model jury (latest Opus + latest GPT + latest Gemini). A mandatory 3-pass floor (line-anchor verification, vendor prior-art, deep prior-art) runs against every Pass 0 lieutenant-seeded candidate; a conditional escalation tier (dataflow + reachability, exploit construction, adversarial red-team disprove) fires on per-finding triggers. Produces FINDINGS.md, JUDGE.md, STATUS.md, severity-sorted master list, and optional PoC + evidence artifacts for that repo. Never uploads or submits anything; all outputs local.
wiki: Generate comprehensive codebase documentation for a repository. Uploads the wiki to view in the Factory app.
wiki-video-gen: Generate Factory-branded HyperFrames video overviews for repository wikis. Use when wiki generation reaches Phase 3.6, or when the user asks for a narrated repository overview video.
install-wiki: Install a CI action that automatically refreshes the Factory Wiki on each push to the default branch. Use when the user wants to set up automated wiki generation, install wiki CI, or configure wiki refresh.
browse-wiki: Search and read wiki documentation for a repository

### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto

This file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.

#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions
*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.
  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the "Snowball" session.
  *   **The Compliance Engine ("Law Firm"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).
*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: "The Sled" (1:1 shared memory layout), "The Shuttle" (the Rust bridge/courier), "The Snowball" (appended session ledger), and "The Strike/Etch" (generating the hash).

#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The "Reality")
*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.
*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).
*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).
*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.

#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules
*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).
*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.
*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).
*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.
*   `docs/`: Reference docs.

#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)

**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**

*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.
*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new("systemctl")`, `Command::new("ip")`, `Command::new("s6-svc")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.
*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.
*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.
*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.
*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.
*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).
*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.
*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.
*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.

#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)

Every D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).

**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`

**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**

| category | what it classifies |
|---|---|
| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |
| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |
| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |
| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |
| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |
| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |
| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |

**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.

**Rules:**
- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`
- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`

- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`
- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`
- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI

**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`

# Design — Generative UI Catalog

## 1. Architecture

```text
 gemma_brain ──mint──▶ CatalogService (gRPC) ──stream──▶ op-web (Rust) ──gRPC-Web──▶ React SPA
                              │                                                          │
                              ▼                                                          ▼
                       catalog store                                              useCatalogStore
                       (authoritative)                                            (Zustand projection)
                                                                                         │
                                                                                         ▼
                                                                                  DSL Interpreter
                                                                                  (json-render.dev)
                                                                                         │
                                                                                         ▼
                                                                                  Shadcn primitives
```

Authoritative state lives in gemma_brain. The frontend is a projection. The interpreter is the only renderer.

## 2. Components

### 2.1 CatalogService (gRPC)
```protobuf
service CatalogService {
  rpc Subscribe(SubscribeRequest) returns (stream CatalogFrame);
  rpc Ack(AckRequest) returns (AckResponse);
}

message SubscribeRequest { string session_id = 1; optional uint64 resume_cursor = 2; }

message CatalogFrame {
  uint64 cursor = 1;
  oneof body {
    Snapshot snapshot = 2;
    Upsert   upsert   = 3;
    Evict    evict    = 4;
    Heartbeat heartbeat = 5;
  }
}

message Element {
  string id = 1;          // content-addressed
  bytes  spec = 2;        // DSL JSON, gzipped
  ElementMeta meta = 3;
}

message ElementMeta {
  string constraint_cocktail_hash = 1;
  uint64 minted_at_ms = 2;
  repeated string forbidden_names_checked = 3; // audit trail
  uint32 dsl_node_count = 4;
}
```

Framing follows the project's custom 5-byte length-prefixed gRPC-Web convention (`mem://tech/communication-protocol`). Routed via Nginx on internal ports 50051/50052 (`mem://tech/grpc-network-routing`).

### 2.2 Catalog store (Rust, op-web)
- Holds the rolling 200-element window.
- Validates incoming `Upsert` against DSL schema; rejected elements never reach the client.
- Enforces the no-name rule by scanning `ElementMeta` and spec strings against the forbidden-names lexicon derived from `mem://features/generative-ui/inspiration-primitives`.
- Persists cursor per session for resume.

### 2.3 useCatalogStore (Zustand)
```ts
interface CatalogState {
  byId: Map<string, Element>;
  order: string[];               // freshness-ordered
  cursor: bigint;
  applyFrame(frame: CatalogFrame): void;  // imperative, no setState in hot path
  get(id: string): Element | undefined;
}
```
- High-frequency `applyFrame` writes through `getState()` to avoid re-renders (`mem://tech/high-frequency-stream-performance`).
- A separate `useCatalogVersion()` selector exposes a monotonic version for components that must subscribe.

### 2.4 DSL Interpreter
- Pure function: `(spec: DslNode, ctx: RenderCtx) => ReactNode`.
- `RenderCtx` provides: masked data accessors, action dispatcher, theme tokens, diagnostics sink.
- Node kinds map to Shadcn primitives (`mem://features/generative-ui`).
- Unknown nodes render a `<DslDiagnostic>` chip with the node kind and element id — never throw.

### 2.5 Mint pipeline (gemma_brain side, summarized)
- For each mint request, build the prompt from the constraint-cocktail scaffold.
- Strip / regenerate on any forbidden-name hit.
- Output validated against DSL JSON schema before publishing to CatalogService.

## 3. Data flow per render

1. Surface declares a `surfaceKey`.
2. Resolver picks an element id from the catalog by `surfaceKey` affinity (round-robin within compatible set).
3. Interpreter renders the spec with a `RenderCtx` bound to that surface.
4. Operator interaction dispatches DSL actions → `useEventStore` → backend mutations.

## 4. Failure modes

| Failure | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Stream disconnect | Reconnect with last cursor; UI keeps last good elements. |
| Empty catalog | Render "awaiting mint" diagnostic surface. |
| Spec validation fail at backend | Element never enters store; logged to reasoning-audit. |
| Unknown DSL node at runtime | Inline diagnostic chip, surrounding spec keeps rendering. |
| Forbidden-name hit | Element rejected pre-publish; gemma re-prompted with stricter constraints. |

## 5. Security

- Masking enforced inside `RenderCtx` accessors — specs cannot bypass.
- DSL has no escape hatch: no raw HTML node, no script node, no fetch node.
- All mutations dispatched through the existing action allowlist.

## 6. Trade-offs accepted

- **Variety over consistency:** operator sees different elements per session. Mitigated by surface-affinity resolver.
- **Interpreter overhead vs. compile-time components:** accepted for zero-deploy iteration.
- **gemma authorship vs. determinism:** accepted; reasoning-audit captures provenance.

# Requirements — Generative UI Catalog

**Feature:** gemma_brain authored, gRPC-streamed catalog of declarative UI elements rendered through a json-render.dev DSL interpreter. Replaces all hand-rolled renderers in the operator console.

**Status:** Draft
**Owner:** AI Agent (authoritative)
**Related memory:** `mem://features/generative-ui/*`, `mem://features/generative-ui/json-render-catalog`, `mem://features/generative-ui/mint-prompt-scaffold`, `mem://features/generative-ui/inspiration-primitives`

---

## 1. User stories

### US-1 — Operator sees novel UI per surface
As an operator, I want each console surface to render with a gemma-authored element so that the interface adapts to the data and task instead of forcing data into pre-made widgets.

**Acceptance:**
- Every render path in the console resolves through the catalog interpreter.
- No component imports a hand-rolled renderer for primary data display.
- Same logical surface may resolve to different elements over time as the gallery rotates.

### US-2 — gemma mints elements without naming patterns
As the system, I want gemma's prompts to forbid known UI pattern names so that minted elements explore the constraint space instead of cloning Miller columns / marking menus / etc.

**Acceptance:**
- Every mint request uses the constraint-cocktail scaffold (`mem://features/generative-ui/mint-prompt-scaffold`).
- Mint requests never contain words from the inspiration-primitives list as solution names.
- gemma output that contains a known pattern name in element metadata is rejected and regenerated.

### US-3 — 200-element rolling gallery
As the system, I want to maintain a rolling gallery of 200 elements so that the operator sees variety and stale elements are evicted.

**Acceptance:**
- Catalog holds exactly 200 active elements at steady state.
- New mints evict oldest / lowest-scoring elements.
- Eviction and insertion stream through the same gRPC channel.

### US-4 — Stream catalog over gRPC
As the frontend, I want catalog state to arrive as a gRPC stream so that I never poll and never hold stale specs.

**Acceptance:**
- One `CatalogService.Subscribe` server-stream per session.
- Frame types: `Snapshot`, `Upsert`, `Evict`, `Heartbeat`.
- Reconnect resumes from cursor without full resnapshot when possible.

### US-5 — Declarative DSL, interpreted not compiled
As the frontend, I want elements expressed as data so that no code reload is needed to ship a new element.

**Acceptance:**
- Element spec is JSON conforming to the json-render.dev DSL schema.
- Interpreter executes spec against live Zustand state.
- Unknown DSL nodes degrade gracefully with a visible diagnostic, not a crash.

### US-6 — No hardcoded mocks
As the codebase, I want zero hand-authored example elements in production paths so that the gallery is always gemma's truth.

**Acceptance:**
- `rg` over `src/` finds no inline DSL literals outside test fixtures.
- Empty catalog state renders an explicit "awaiting mint" diagnostic, not a placeholder element.

---

## 2. Non-functional requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| NFR-1 | Interpreter renders a 200-node spec in <16ms on the operator workstation. |
| NFR-2 | High-frequency stream updates use imperative `useEventStore.getState()` — no per-frame React re-renders. |
| NFR-3 | All rendering paths honor the masking rules in `mem://features/security-masking`. |
| NFR-4 | Catalog stream survives gRPC reconnect without losing operator focus on the current element. |
| NFR-5 | DSL interpreter is sandboxed: no `eval`, no DOM escape, no network calls from spec. |

## 3. Out of scope

- Operator-authored elements (gemma-only for now).
- Cross-session persistence of operator preferences per element.
- A/B scoring infrastructure (separate spec).

## 4. Open questions

- Eviction policy: pure FIFO, or weighted by operator dwell / interaction?
- Should `Snapshot` frames be diffable, or always full 200?
- Do we expose mint provenance (prompt seed, constraint cocktail) in the element metadata for the reasoning-audit surface?

Ordered. Each task is independently shippable behind a feature flag until T-12 flips the default.

## Open decisions before T-2 / T-5

- Eviction policy: FIFO vs. weighted (block on product decision).
- Snapshot diffability (block on T-5 implementation choice).
- Mint provenance exposure in audit (block on T-21).

# Design — Operator Console Topology

## 1. Topology

```text
                    Operator workstation
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   zeroclaw-gui  (native eframe/egui)      │
        │   - tokio runtime                         │
        │   - tonic-web gRPC client                 │
        │   - prost-reflect DescriptorPool          │
        │   - schemars-driven UI renderer           │
        │   - embedded Chat panel (AI SDK bridge)   │
        └───────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                        │ gRPC-Web (HTTP/1.1, 5-byte framing)
                        │ + ServerReflection bootstrap
                        ▼
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   nginx reverse proxy                     │
        │   :50051 / :50052 → op-web                │
        └───────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                        ▼
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   op-web (Rust, tonic + tower)            │
        │   - tonic-web GrpcWebLayer                │
        │   - tonic_reflection                      │
        │   - op-plugins services                   │
        │   - SSE/WS sidecar (high-freq state)      │
        │   - ChatService (AI SDK bridge, server)   │
        └───────┬─────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                │             │
                ▼             ▼
         D-Bus mirror     gemma_brain
         (1:1 truth)      (projections:
                           gallery, reasoning,
                           persona registry)
                │
                ▼
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ Backplane                                 │
        │  Qdrant @ 10.149.181.190:6334             │
        │  Blockchain audit · Embedding worker      │
        │  s6/s6-rc supervision (Artix)             │
        │  WireGuard / XRay / WARP mesh             │
        │  Identity sled (WG pubkey → RBAC)         │
        └───────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 2. Two-system split

| Surface | Role | Runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `lovable/` | Design workspace: theme, nav, widget prototyping | React 18 + Vite + Tailwind |
| `lovable/.zeroclaw/` | Operator runtime (`zeroclaw-gui`) | Rust + eframe/egui + tokio |

The React workspace exists to iterate visuals and schema-driven widgets quickly. It is not the product. The `op-web` SPA handlers and rust-embed of Vite `dist/` are removed in this spec.

## 3. `zeroclaw-gui` elements

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `main.rs` | eframe entry, tokio multi-thread runtime, `grpc::bootstrap` against `ZEROCLAW_GRPC` |
| `app.rs` | Shell: topbar + collapsible sidebar + routed content; holds `ReflectionRegistry`, `InvokeHandle`, `ExplorerState`, theme, connection |
| `nav.rs` | `Route` enum + `NAV_GROUPS`, mirrors the React nav 1:1 |
| `theme.rs` | Graphite/slate dark tokens, red accents, Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono |
| `grpc.rs` | tonic-web `Channel`, `ServerReflectionClient`, `DescriptorPool`, `decode_to_json` |
| `schema.rs` | `(schemars::Schema, serde_json::Value) → egui` recursive renderer |
| `views/` | Schema-driven views: Inspector, State, gRPC, gRPC Explorer, Logs, etc. |
| `chat/` | New module — Antigravity-style embedded chat panel (see §5) |

## 4. Technologies & protocols

**Native client:** eframe 0.28, egui 0.28, tokio, hyper 1, http, tower, tonic 0.12, tonic-web 0.12, tonic-reflection 0.12, prost 0.13, prost-reflect 0.14, serde, schemars 1.0, release profile with thin LTO.

**Backplane:** Qdrant, blockchain audit, embedding worker, s6/s6-rc on Artix, WireGuard/XRay/WARP, identity sled (WG-pubkey → RBAC), D-Bus mirror. **No Supabase at runtime** — Lovable Cloud is provisioned but unused; no tables, auth, edge functions, or storage are reached from app code.

**Protocols:**
- gRPC-Web over HTTP/1.1 with custom 5-byte length-prefixed framing (`mem://tech/communication-protocol`).
- gRPC ServerReflection v1.
- Schema-as-code (`schemars`) contract for payload shape.
- Hybrid unary/server-stream + SSE/WS sidecar for high-frequency state (`mem://features/streaming`).
- D-Bus mirror for 1:1 host-state sync (`mem://tech/grpc-dbus-mirror-architecture`).

## 5. Embedded Chat (Antigravity-style)

The chat panel lives **inside** `zeroclaw-gui` as the `Chat` route, the way Antigravity embeds its agent in the IDE shell. It is not a separate window or a browser popup.

**Hosting:** all inference happens on our own infrastructure (`gemma_brain` model runtime fronted by `op-web`). **Lovable AI Gateway is not used.** No `LOVABLE_API_KEY`, no `ai.gateway.lovable.dev`, no third-party hosted models. The AI SDK provider helper is removed.

### 5.1 Server side (`op-web` ChatService)

- New gRPC service `ChatService` with:
  - `Send(SendRequest) returns (stream ChatFrame)` — streams `UIMessagePart` events as binary-framed gRPC-Web frames.
- Inference is performed by `gemma_brain` directly; `op-web` is the gRPC façade and tool dispatcher.
- Tool catalog defined in Rust (typed argument schemas via `schemars`), each tool wraps an existing `op-plugins` RPC.
- Mutating tools require explicit approval; approval round-trips through the chat panel via `ChatService.Approve`.
- Agent loop is bounded (≥50 steps) and cancellable via `ChatService.Cancel`.
- System prompt, tool catalog, and persona come from `gemma_brain`'s persona registry stream.
- The wire shape mirrors the AI SDK `UIMessage` part vocabulary (text / tool-call / tool-result / reasoning) so renderers stay portable, but the producer is our own runtime — no AI SDK `streamText` / `toUIMessageStreamResponse` call exists on the server.

### 5.2 Native client side (`zeroclaw-gui/src/chat/`)

- `chat::transport` — subscribes to `ChatService.Send`, decodes `ChatFrame` → `UIMessagePart`, pushes into `chat::store`.
- `chat::store` — append-only `Vec<UIMessage>` keyed by conversation id; imperative writes via `getState()`-equivalent to avoid egui repaint storms on token bursts.
- `chat::view` — egui composition with AI-Elements-shaped semantics (renderer parity only, not transport parity):
  - Conversation transcript with sticky-to-bottom + scroll affordance.
  - Per-message role styling: assistant text on the page surface (no bubble); user messages in a high-contrast token pair.
  - Streamed markdown for assistant text.
  - Tool parts: name + status + domain icon, input collapsed by default, compact output.
  - Composer: persistent focus, "Thinking…" indicator during `submitted`.
  - Identity: domain-specific `gemma_brain` glyph, not `Sparkles`.

### 5.3 React workspace mirror (design only)

- `lovable/src/routes/chat` composes AI Elements (`Conversation`, `Message`, `MessageResponse`, `PromptInput`, `Tool*`, `Shimmer`) **as renderers only**, pointed at the same gRPC `ChatService` (via grpc-web in the browser) so visual choices iterate against real traffic.
- No Lovable AI Gateway provider, no `/api/chat` Edge Function pointing at `ai.gateway.lovable.dev`, no `LOVABLE_API_KEY` reads in the React workspace.
- Conversation shape & storage choice is gathered with `questions--ask_questions` before any chat file is created (`chat-agent-ui-contract`).

### 5.4 Conversation/storage

Per `chat-agent-ui-contract`, two orthogonal choices must be answered before build:
- **Shape:** threaded vs. single.
- **Storage:** Rust-side sled/disk under the operator's XDG data dir (native), `localStorage` (design workspace mirror), or none. **Supabase is not an option** — see §7.

If threaded + persisted, threads have real routes (`/$threadId` in TanStack, `/chat/:threadId` in Classic) and a stable native `Route::Chat(thread_id)` in egui.

### 5.5 Lovable AI disconnection

- Project-level Lovable AI Gateway is disconnected; `LOVABLE_API_KEY` is removed from project secrets.
- Any pre-existing `src/lib/ai-gateway*`, `supabase/functions/chat`, or `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider code is deleted.
- The repo README states explicitly: **all model inference is self-hosted in `gemma_brain`; no external AI gateway is in use.**

## 6. Failure modes

| Failure | Behavior |
|---|---|
| gRPC bootstrap fails | Console renders connection diagnostic surface; retries with backoff. |
| Reflection missing a descriptor | Affected view shows labeled diagnostic; other views unaffected. |
| Chat stream disconnect | Last good transcript preserved; retry with cursor; UI shows reconnecting state. |
| Tool error | Inline tool card flips to error state with compact error payload; transcript continues. |
| `gemma_brain` inference unavailable / overloaded | ChatService returns explicit error frame; UI surfaces actionable status (queue depth, retry hint). |
| Masking violation attempt | Accessor refuses; reasoning-audit records attempt. |

## 7. Security

- **Identity** = caller's WireGuard public key, stored in the identity sled inside the Rust stack (`mem://auth/wireguard-identity`). No JWT, no Supabase auth, no OAuth, no bearer tokens on the wire.
- **Authorization** = RBAC lookup against the identity sled, enforced server-side in `op-web`.
- Chat tools execute server-side only; client cannot invoke arbitrary RPCs through chat.
- Approval-gated tools require explicit operator confirmation in the chat UI.
- All chat tool calls + results recorded in the blockchain audit pipeline (`mem://features/security/audit-and-search`).
- No model traffic ever leaves the operator network — there is no outbound call to a hosted AI gateway.
- **No Supabase at runtime** (`mem://constraints/no-supabase-runtime-use`): no `public` tables, RLS policies, edge functions, or storage buckets are read or written by the application.

## 8. Trade-offs accepted

- **Native-only runtime** vs. browser convenience — accepted; operator workflow demands it.
- **Self-hosted inference** vs. managed AI gateway — accepted; data sovereignty and offline operation outrank managed convenience. We give up the AI SDK ecosystem (`streamText`, provider switching) but keep its `UIMessage` wire vocabulary so renderers stay portable.
- **Two design surfaces (React + egui)** vs. one — accepted as design workspace cost; offset by shared schema/DSL contracts.

# Requirements — Operator Console Topology

**Feature:** Native `zeroclaw-gui` operator console as the sole runtime, with `lovable/` React SPA demoted to a design workspace, and an Antigravity-IDE-style embedded chat agent (AI SDK + Lovable AI Gateway) as the primary operator-to-system interface.

**Status:** Draft
**Owner:** AI Agent (authoritative)
**Related memory:** `mem://tech/architecture`, `mem://tech/communication-protocol`, `mem://tech/grpc-dbus-mirror-architecture`, `mem://tech/grpc-network-routing`, `mem://tech/state-projection-store`, `mem://features/streaming`, `mem://features/grpc-diagnostics`, `mem://features/generative-ui/json-render-catalog`

---

## 1. User stories

### US-1 — Single operator runtime
As an operator, I want one native console (`zeroclaw-gui`) that runs out-of-browser so that I am not subject to browser sandbox limits, tab lifecycle, or JS GC pauses during incident response.

**Acceptance:**
- `zeroclaw-gui` is the only artifact shipped to operator workstations.
- The React SPA is not published as a production surface.
- Vite preview exists for design iteration only and is clearly labeled as such.

### US-2 — React workspace is design-only
As the AI Agent, I want `lovable/` retained as a prototyping sandbox so that views, theme tokens, nav layout, and schema-driven widgets can be iterated quickly before porting to egui.

**Acceptance:**
- `lovable/` contains no production business logic.
- Every component in `lovable/` has a counterpart or design-only marker.
- README at repo root states the two-system split.

### US-3 — gRPC-Web as the only client transport
As the system, I want all client/server traffic over gRPC-Web with binary 5-byte framing so that protocol shape is uniform across native and (legacy) browser clients.

**Acceptance:**
- No REST endpoints in the production path of `op-web`.
- All RPCs are reachable via `ServerReflection`.
- High-frequency streams use the SSE/WS sidecar documented in `mem://features/streaming`.

### US-4 — Schema-as-code contract
As the renderer, I want every payload describable by a `schemars` Schema so that UI rendering is generic and does not require per-message code.

**Acceptance:**
- Every plugin state struct derives `schemars::JsonSchema`.
- `schema.rs` renders any `(Schema, Value)` pair without crashing.
- Unknown schema constructs degrade to a labeled diagnostic frame, never a raw JSON dump outside one.

### US-5 — gemma_brain owns projections
As the system, I want `gemma_brain` to be the projection owner for gallery, reasoning, and persona registry so that the client never recomputes derived state.

**Acceptance:**
- No client-side derivation of gallery or persona state.
- Projections stream through gRPC; `zeroclaw-gui` mirrors into `useEventStore`-equivalent stores.
- D-Bus mirror stays 1:1 with gRPC truth (`mem://tech/grpc-dbus-mirror-architecture`).

### US-6 — Strip SPA-only paths from `op-web`
As the codebase, I want `op-web` free of SPA-only handlers so that the cutover to native-only is real and not a parallel deployment.

**Acceptance:**
- `handlers/gemma.rs`, `handlers/ui_gallery.rs`, `/api/gemma/*`, and rust-embed of Vite `dist/` removed.
- `op-web` binary size drops accordingly.
- CI gate prevents reintroduction of SPA-only routes.

### US-7 — Embedded chat agent (Antigravity-style)
As an operator, I want a chat surface embedded directly into the console — the same way Antigravity puts an agent panel inside the IDE — so that I can converse with `gemma_brain`, invoke tools, watch streamed tool activity, and stay in one window.

**Acceptance:**
- A dedicated `Chat` route in `nav.rs` opens a persistent panel inside `zeroclaw-gui`.
- The chat surface is served entirely by our own server-side AI in `gemma_brain` / `op-web` — **no Lovable AI Gateway, no third-party hosted inference, no `LOVABLE_API_KEY`**.
- Wire format follows the AI SDK `UIMessage` part shape (text, tool-call, tool-result, reasoning) so the renderer stays interchangeable, but the producer is our own model runtime, not the AI SDK provider library.
- Tool activity renders inline with status, collapsible input, and compact output (closed by default).
- The composer stays focused by default; submit disabled while `submitted`/`streaming`.
- Conversation shape and storage are chosen via `questions--ask_questions` per `chat-agent-ui-contract` before implementation.
- Assistant identity uses a domain-specific mark — never the generic `Sparkles` icon.

### US-8 — No hand-rolled chat renderers
As the codebase, I want the chat UI assembled from one set of primitives (AI Elements-shaped in the React workspace, egui-shaped in `zeroclaw-gui`) so that the experience is consistent across surfaces.

**Acceptance:**
- React workspace chat composes `Conversation`, `Message`, `MessageResponse`, `PromptInput`, `Tool*`, `Shimmer` from AI Elements **as renderers only**, pointed at our gRPC `ChatService` — not any Lovable endpoint.
- Native chat in `zeroclaw-gui` consumes the same `UIMessagePart` stream over gRPC-Web framing.
- No bespoke transcript, tool accordion, or composer outside those renderers.

### US-9 — Disconnect Lovable AI features
As the project, I want Lovable AI / AI Gateway features explicitly disabled so that nothing in the codebase implies external model hosting.

**Acceptance:**
- `LOVABLE_API_KEY` is not referenced by any production code path.
- Lovable AI Gateway is disconnected at the project level; the manual disconnect step is documented in the repo README.
- Any leftover `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider helper, `ai-gateway.server.ts`, or Lovable-gateway-pointed `/api/chat` routes are deleted.
- CI gate rejects reintroduction of `ai.gateway.lovable.dev`, `Lovable-API-Key`, or `createLovableAiGatewayProvider`.

---

## 2. Non-functional requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| NFR-1 | Cold-start of `zeroclaw-gui` to first rendered frame < 500ms on operator workstation. |
| NFR-2 | gRPC-Web bootstrap (reflection + descriptor pool load) < 1s on LAN. |
| NFR-3 | Schema renderer handles ≥10k-node payloads via virtualization without dropping frames. |
| NFR-4 | High-frequency streams update store imperatively (no per-frame React/egui repaint storm). |
| NFR-5 | Chat tokens stream end-to-end with <150ms p50 first-token latency on Lovable AI Gateway. |
| NFR-6 | Masking rules (`mem://features/security-masking`) enforced on every rendered payload, including tool results in chat. |
| NFR-7 | Native binary contains no JS runtime, no Chromium, no webview. |

## 3. Out of scope

- Mobile or tablet operator console.
- Multi-operator collaborative editing inside the chat panel.
- A/B routing between models (deferred to a separate spec).

## 4. Open questions

- Chat conversation shape: threaded or single? (must be answered via `questions--ask_questions` before T-Chat-1).
- Chat persistence: database (Supabase, RLS-scoped), localStorage equivalent, or none?
- Should tool approval (`needsApproval`) gate destructive backplane ops by default?
- Does the React workspace ship a publishable chat preview, or is chat native-only?

## Spec Review: `lovable/.specs/`

Two specs found. Both are Draft status, authored by the AI Agent role, and reference `mem://` memory anchors throughout.

---

### 1. `generative-ui-catalog` (4 files, ~14 KB)

**Purpose:** A gemma_brain-authored catalog of 200 declarative UI elements streamed over gRPC, replacing all hand-rolled renderers in the operator console. Elements are minted under constraint-cocktail prompts that forbid naming known UI patterns (Miller columns, marking menus, etc.) to force novel explorations of the design space.

**Strengths:**
- Clean separation: gemma_brain owns minting, CatalogService (Rust/op-web) owns authoritative store + validation, React SPA consumes via gRPC-Web with Zustand imperative store.
- DSL is sandboxed by construction: no `html`, `script`, `fetch` node kinds. Masking enforced in `RenderCtx` accessors, never bypassable from spec.
- Failure-mode table is thorough (stream disconnect, empty catalog, validation fail, unknown node, forbidden-name hit).
- Task list is granular and ordered (23 tasks) with feature-flag gating through T-12.

**Concerns:**
- **NFR-1 (<16ms render for 200-node spec)** is stated but uninstrumented. T-22 is the benchmark gate, but no target hardware profile is specified. "Operator workstation" is vague.
- **Eviction policy is an open question** but blocks T-2 and T-5 per the tasks file. The spec should either commit to FIFO-as-stub with weighted as a follow-up, or resolve this before implementation begins.
- **`Snapshot` frame diffability** is also open. If always-full-200, bandwidth is trivial on LAN but wasteful on degraded links. No size estimate for a gzipped 200-element snapshot is given.
- **Forbidden-names lexicon** loader (T-4) has no source-of-truth defined beyond a `mem://` anchor. If that memory entry is missing or stale, the rejection loop has no fallback.
- **`surfaceKey` affinity** (§3, data flow) says "round-robin within compatible set" but "compatible" is undefined. What makes an element compatible with a surface? This is a contract gap.
- **T-17 CI gate** (`rg` for DSL literals outside `__fixtures__/`) is good but doesn't address the transition period where hand-rolled renderers still exist behind the flag.

**Verdict:** Solid architectural spec. Resolves the eviction policy, surface-affinity contract, and snapshot diffability before T-2/T-5 and this is ready to build.

---

### 2. `operator-console-topology` (4 files, ~32 KB)

**Purpose:** Establishes `zeroclaw-gui` (native eframe/egui Rust app) as the sole operator runtime, demotes `lovable/` React SPA to design-only, strips SPA handlers from `op-web`, and embeds an Antigravity-style chat agent powered by self-hosted `gemma_brain` inference (no Lovable AI Gateway, no external hosted models).

**Strengths:**
- Topology diagram is clear and matches AGENTS.md architecture (D-Bus mirror, Qdrant backplane, WireGuard identity, s6 supervision).
- ChatService contract re-encodes AI SDK SSE into binary `ChatFrame` events. Wire vocabulary mirrors `UIMessage` part kinds for renderer portability without a runtime AI SDK dependency. This is a clean decoupling.
- Lovable AI disconnection is thorough: T-Disco-1 through T-Disco-5 with CI gate rejecting reintroduction of gateway strings. Aligns with the "self-hosted inference" stance in AGENTS.md.
- Two-system split (React design workspace + native runtime) is well-justified with shared schema/DSL contracts as the bridge.
- Security model (WireGuard pubkey identity, RBAC via identity sled, no JWT/Supabase auth) is consistent with the codebase rules.

**Concerns:**
- **NFR-5 references "Lovable AI Gateway"** for the <150ms first-token latency target, but the spec simultaneously removes the Lovable AI Gateway. This is a copy-paste artifact. The NFR should reference `gemma_brain` on the operator LAN.
- **T-Chat-6 (Supabase storage)** contradicts the spec's own §7 ("No Supabase at runtime") and the `mem://constraints/no-supabase-runtime-use` constraint. The task says "If storage = database: Supabase tables..." but the design explicitly rules out Supabase. This task should either be removed or rewritten to use sled/disk or a Rust-native store.
- **Open question "Chat persistence: database (Supabase, RLS-scoped)..."** lists Supabase as an option, but §5.4 and §7 both say Supabase is not an option. The open-questions section needs to be reconciled with the constraints.
- **NFR-3 (10k-node payload virtualization)** is ambitious for egui. egui's immediate-mode architecture makes virtualization patterns different from DOM. T-3 and T-P2 reference this but no egui-specific virtualization strategy is described.
- **`prost-reflect` DescriptorPool as single source of truth** for decoding is elegant but the spec doesn't address pool invalidation when the server adds new services at runtime. Does the client re-reflection periodically? On reconnect only?
- **T-Chat-0 blocks all chat tasks** on the `questions--ask_questions` answer for conversation shape + storage. This is a hard gate that should be resolved before any chat work begins. The spec should either pre-commit to answers or flag this as the immediate next action.
- **`chat::store` uses imperative writes** to avoid repaint storms, which is correct for egui, but the spec doesn't describe the repaint request strategy. egui requires explicit `ctx.request_repaint()` calls; the spec should specify when repaints are requested (per-frame? throttled?).
- **React workspace chat mirror (T-Chat-16 through T-Chat-19)** is marked design-only but still wires to the real gRPC ChatService. If it's truly design-only, should it use a mock stream instead of real traffic? The spec says "pointed at the same gRPC ChatService... so visual choices iterate against real traffic" which is reasonable but means the React workspace is not fully isolated.

**Verdict:** Comprehensive and well-aligned with the codebase architecture. The critical blockers are: (1) fix the NFR-5 Lovable Gateway reference, (2) reconcile the Supabase contradiction between T-Chat-6/open-questions and §5.4/§7, and (3) resolve T-Chat-0's questions before any chat implementation begins. The egui virtualization strategy (NFR-3) also needs a concrete design before T-3.

**Protocols:**
- gRPC-Web over HTTP/1.1 with custom 5-byte length-prefixed framing (`mem://tech/communication-protocol`).
- gRPC ServerReflection v1.
- Schema-as-code (`schemars`) contract for payload shape.
- Hybrid unary/server-stream + SSE/WS sidecar for high-frequency state (`mem://features/streaming`).
- D-Bus mirror for 1:1 host-state sync (`mem://tech/grpc-dbus-mirror-architecture`).

### 4.1 egui virtualization strategy

egui is immediate-mode; virtualization is done by rendering only the visible row range, not by offscreen DOM nodes.

- `schema::render_array` uses `egui::ScrollArea::show_rows(height, |range| { ... })` to iterate only the visible slice of large arrays. The row height is computed from the first N items and cached; heterogeneous heights fall back to a fixed estimate with a correction pass.
- For tree-structured payloads (`object` with nested `properties`), an expanded-rows cache (`ExplorerState`) flattens the visible tree into a `Vec<RowHandle>` per frame. Only the visible range of that vector is rendered.
- `ctx.request_repaint()` is called only on scroll events and stream updates, not on every frame. Idle surfaces do not request repaint.
- The `RowHandle` indirection means schema resolution + data lookup happens for visible rows only; a 10k-node payload with 50 visible rows does O(50) work per frame, not O(10k).

- Hybrid unary/server-stream + SSE/WS sidecar for high-frequency state (`mem://features/streaming`).
- D-Bus mirror for 1:1 host-state sync (`mem://tech/grpc-dbus-mirror-architecture`).

### 4.1 egui virtualization strategy

egui is immediate-mode; virtualization is done by rendering only the visible row range, not by offscreen DOM nodes.

- `schema::render_array` uses `egui::ScrollArea::show_rows(height, |range| { ... })` to iterate only the visible slice of large arrays. The row height is computed from the first N items and cached; heterogeneous heights fall back to a fixed estimate with a correction pass.
- For tree-structured payloads (`object` with nested `properties`), an expanded-rows cache (`ExplorerState`) flattens the visible tree into a `Vec<RowHandle>` per frame. Only the visible range of that vector is rendered.
- `ctx.request_repaint()` is called only on scroll events and stream updates, not on every frame. Idle surfaces do not request repaint.
- The `RowHandle` indirection means schema resolution + data lookup happens for visible rows only; a 10k-node payload with 50 visible rows does O(50) work per frame, not O(10k).

## 5. Embedded Chat (Antigravity-style)

The chat panel lives **inside** `zeroclaw-gui` as the `Chat` route, the way Antigravity embeds its agent in the IDE shell. It is not a separate window or a browser popup.

**Hosting:** all inference happens on our own infrastructure (`gemma_brain` model runtime fronted by `op-web`). **Lovable AI Gateway is not used.** No `LOVABLE_API_KEY`, no `ai.gateway.lovable.dev`, no third-party hosted models. The AI SDK provider helper is removed.

### 5.1 Server side (`op-web` ChatService)

- New gRPC service `ChatService` with:
  - `Send(SendRequest) returns (stream ChatFrame)` — streams `UIMessagePart` events as binary-framed gRPC-Web frames.
- Inference is performed by `gemma_brain` directly; `op-web` is the gRPC façade and tool dispatcher.
- Tool catalog defined in Rust (typed argument schemas via `schemars`), each tool wraps an existing `op-plugins` RPC.
- Mutating tools require explicit approval; approval round-trips through the chat panel via `ChatService.Approve`.
- Agent loop is bounded (≥50 steps) and cancellable via `ChatService.Cancel`.
- System prompt, tool catalog, and persona come from `gemma_brain`'s persona registry stream.
- The wire shape mirrors the AI SDK `UIMessage` part vocabulary (text / tool-call / tool-result / reasoning) so renderers stay portable, but the producer is our own runtime — no AI SDK `streamText` / `toUIMessageStreamResponse` call exists on the server.

### 5.2 Native client side (`zeroclaw-gui/src/chat/`)

- `chat::transport` — subscribes to `ChatService.Send`, decodes `ChatFrame` → `UIMessagePart`, pushes into `chat::store`.
- `chat::store` — append-only `Vec<UIMessage>` keyed by conversation id; imperative writes via `getState()`-equivalent to avoid egui repaint storms on token bursts.
- `chat::view` — egui composition with AI-Elements-shaped semantics (renderer parity only, not transport parity):
  - Conversation transcript with sticky-to-bottom + scroll affordance.
  - Per-message role styling: assistant text on the page surface (no bubble); user messages in a high-contrast token pair.
  - Streamed markdown for assistant text.
  - Tool parts: name + status + domain icon, input collapsed by default, compact output.
  - Composer: persistent focus, "Thinking…" indicator during `submitted`.
  - Identity: domain-specific `gemma_brain` glyph, not `Sparkles`.

### 5.3 Conversation/storage

Conversation persistence is handled by the **memory loop** (`mem://features/memory-loop`) backed by **cognitive-mcp** (`100.90.37.254:3003`). No Supabase, no browser localStorage, no XDG JSON files.

- **Memory loop** owns the conversation lifecycle: append, recall, summarization, eviction. Chat transcripts are fed into the loop as `evt.*` records and recalled by semantic search through cognitive-mcp's Qdrant-backed memory tools.
- **cognitive-mcp** is the persistence gateway. The native client never writes chat state to disk directly; it dispatches memory-store actions through the existing gRPC → D-Bus → cognitive-mcp path.
- Conversation shape (threaded vs. single) is still gathered via `questions--ask_questions` before implementation, but storage is settled: memory loop + cognitive-mcp, always.
- If threaded, `thread_id` is a cognitive-mcp memory key, not a database row ID. Native route is `Route::Chat(thread_id)` in `nav.rs`.

- If threaded, `thread_id` is a cognitive-mcp memory key, not a database row ID. Native route is `Route::Chat(thread_id)` in `nav.rs`.

### 5.4 Lovable AI disconnection

- Project-level Lovable AI Gateway is disconnected; `LOVABLE_API_KEY` is removed from project secrets.
- Any pre-existing `src/lib/ai-gateway*`, `supabase/functions/chat`, or `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider code is deleted.
- The repo README states explicitly: **all model inference is self-hosted in `gemma_brain`; no external AI gateway is in use.**

## 6. Failure modes

| Failure | Behavior |
|---|---|
| gRPC bootstrap fails | Console renders connection diagnostic surface; retries with backoff. |
| Reflection missing a descriptor | Affected view shows labeled diagnostic; other views unaffected. |
| Chat stream disconnect | Last good transcript preserved; retry with cursor; UI shows reconnecting state. |
| Tool error | Inline tool card flips to error state with compact error payload; transcript continues. |
| `gemma_brain` inference unavailable / overloaded | ChatService returns explicit error frame; UI surfaces actionable status (queue depth, retry hint). |
| Masking violation attempt | Accessor refuses; reasoning-audit records attempt. |

## 7. Security

- **Identity** = caller's WireGuard public key, stored in the identity sled inside the Rust stack (`mem://auth/wireguard-identity`). No JWT, no Supabase auth, no OAuth, no bearer tokens on the wire.
- **Authorization** = RBAC lookup against the identity sled, enforced server-side in `op-web`.
- Chat tools execute server-side only; client cannot invoke arbitrary RPCs through chat.
- Approval-gated tools require explicit operator confirmation in the chat UI.
- All chat tool calls + results recorded in the blockchain audit pipeline (`mem://features/security/audit-and-search`).
- No model traffic ever leaves the operator network — there is no outbound call to a hosted AI gateway.
- **No Supabase at runtime** (`mem://constraints/no-supabase-runtime-use`): no `public` tables, RLS policies, edge functions, or storage buckets are read or written by the application.

## 8. Trade-offs accepted

- **Native-only runtime** vs. browser convenience — accepted; operator workflow demands it.
- **Self-hosted inference** vs. managed AI gateway — accepted; data sovereignty and offline operation outrank managed convenience. We give up the AI SDK ecosystem (`streamText`, provider switching) but keep its `UIMessage` wire vocabulary so renderers stay portable.
- **Two design surfaces (React + egui)** vs. one — accepted as design workspace cost; offset by shared schema/DSL contracts.

# Design — Operator Console Topology

## 1. Topology

```text
                    Operator workstation
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   zeroclaw-gui  (native eframe/egui)      │
        │   - tokio runtime                         │
        │   - tonic-web gRPC client                 │
        │   - prost-reflect DescriptorPool          │
        │   - schemars-driven UI renderer           │
        │   - embedded Chat panel (gemma_brain)     │
        └───────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                        │ gRPC-Web (HTTP/1.1, 5-byte framing)
                        │ + ServerReflection bootstrap
                        ▼
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   nginx reverse proxy                     │
        │   :50051 / :50052 → op-web                │
        └───────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                        ▼
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   op-web (Rust, tonic + tower)            │
        │   - tonic-web GrpcWebLayer                │
        │   - tonic_reflection                      │
        │   - op-plugins services                   │
        │   - SSE/WS sidecar (high-freq state)      │
        │   - ChatService (gemma_brain façade)      │
        └───────┬─────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                │             │
                ▼             ▼
         D-Bus mirror     gemma_brain
         (1:1 truth)      (projections:
                           gallery, reasoning,
                           persona registry)
                │
                ▼
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ Backplane                                 │
        │  Qdrant @ 10.149.181.190:6334             │
        │  Blockchain audit · Embedding worker      │
        │  s6/s6-rc supervision (Artix)             │
        │  WireGuard / XRay / WARP mesh             │
        │  Identity sled (WG pubkey → RBAC)         │
        └───────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 2. Two-system split

| Surface | Role | Runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `lovable/` | Design workspace: theme, nav, widget prototyping (no chat) | React 18 + Vite + Tailwind |
| `lovable/.zeroclaw/` | Operator runtime (`zeroclaw-gui`) | Rust + eframe/egui + tokio |

The React workspace exists to iterate visuals and schema-driven widgets quickly. It is not the product. The `op-web` SPA handlers and rust-embed of Vite `dist/` are removed in this spec.

## 3. `zeroclaw-gui` elements

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `main.rs` | eframe entry, tokio multi-thread runtime, `grpc::bootstrap` against `ZEROCLAW_GRPC` |
| `app.rs` | Shell: topbar + collapsible sidebar + routed content; holds `ReflectionRegistry`, `InvokeHandle`, `ExplorerState`, theme, connection |
| `nav.rs` | `Route` enum + `NAV_GROUPS`, mirrors the React nav 1:1 |
| `theme.rs` | Graphite/slate dark tokens, red accents, Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono |
| `grpc.rs` | tonic-web `Channel`, `ServerReflectionClient`, `DescriptorPool`, `decode_to_json` |
| `schema.rs` | `(schemars::Schema, serde_json::Value) → egui` recursive renderer |
| `views/` | Schema-driven views: Inspector, State, gRPC, gRPC Explorer, Logs, etc. |
| `chat/` | New module — Antigravity-style embedded chat panel (see §5) |

## 4. Technologies & protocols

**Native client:** eframe 0.28, egui 0.28, tokio, hyper 1, http, tower, tonic 0.12, tonic-web 0.12, tonic-reflection 0.12, prost 0.13, prost-reflect 0.14, serde, schemars 1.0, release profile with thin LTO.

**Backplane:** Qdrant, blockchain audit, embedding worker, s6/s6-rc on Artix, WireGuard/XRay/WARP, identity sled (WG-pubkey → RBAC), D-Bus mirror. **No Supabase at runtime** — Lovable Cloud is provisioned but unused; no tables, auth, edge functions, or storage are reached from app code.

**Protocols:**
- gRPC-Web over HTTP/1.1 with custom 5-byte length-prefixed framing (`mem://tech/communication-protocol`).
- gRPC ServerReflection v1.
- Schema-as-code (`schemars`) contract for payload shape.
- Hybrid unary/server-stream + SSE/WS sidecar for high-frequency state (`mem://features/streaming`).
- D-Bus mirror for 1:1 host-state sync (`mem://tech/grpc-dbus-mirror-architecture`).

### 4.1 egui virtualization strategy

egui is immediate-mode; virtualization is done by rendering only the visible row range, not by offscreen DOM nodes.

- `schema::render_array` uses `egui::ScrollArea::show_rows(height, |range| { ... })` to iterate only the visible slice of large arrays. The row height is computed from the first N items and cached; heterogeneous heights fall back to a fixed estimate with a correction pass.
- For tree-structured payloads (`object` with nested `properties`), an expanded-rows cache (`ExplorerState`) flattens the visible tree into a `Vec<RowHandle>` per frame. Only the visible range of that vector is rendered.
- `ctx.request_repaint()` is called only on scroll events and stream updates, not on every frame. Idle surfaces do not request repaint.
- The `RowHandle` indirection means schema resolution + data lookup happens for visible rows only; a 10k-node payload with 50 visible rows does O(50) work per frame, not O(10k).

## 5. Embedded Chat (Antigravity-style)

The chat panel lives **inside** `zeroclaw-gui` as the `Chat` route, the way Antigravity embeds its agent in the IDE shell. It is not a separate window or a browser popup.

**Hosting:** all inference happens on our own infrastructure (`gemma_brain` model runtime fronted by `op-web`). **Lovable AI Gateway is not used.** No `LOVABLE_API_KEY`, no `ai.gateway.lovable.dev`, no third-party hosted models. The AI SDK provider helper is removed.

### 5.1 Server side (`op-web` ChatService)

- New gRPC service `ChatService` with:
  - `Send(SendRequest) returns (stream ChatFrame)` — streams `UIMessagePart` events as binary-framed gRPC-Web frames.
- Inference is performed by `gemma_brain` directly; `op-web` is the gRPC façade and tool dispatcher.
- Tool catalog defined in Rust (typed argument schemas via `schemars`), each tool wraps an existing `op-plugins` RPC.
- Mutating tools require explicit approval; approval round-trips through the chat panel via `ChatService.Approve`.
- Agent loop is bounded (≥50 steps) and cancellable via `ChatService.Cancel`.
- System prompt, tool catalog, and persona come from `gemma_brain`'s persona registry stream.
- The wire shape mirrors the AI SDK `UIMessage` part vocabulary (text / tool-call / tool-result / reasoning) so renderers stay portable, but the producer is our own runtime — no AI SDK `streamText` / `toUIMessageStreamResponse` call exists on the server.

### 5.2 Native client side (`zeroclaw-gui/src/chat/`)

- `chat::transport` — subscribes to `ChatService.Send`, decodes `ChatFrame` → `UIMessagePart`, pushes into `chat::store`.
- `chat::store` — append-only `Vec<UIMessage>` keyed by conversation id; imperative writes via `getState()`-equivalent to avoid egui repaint storms on token bursts.
- `chat::view` — egui composition with AI-Elements-shaped semantics (renderer parity only, not transport parity):
  - Conversation transcript with sticky-to-bottom + scroll affordance.
  - Per-message role styling: assistant text on the page surface (no bubble); user messages in a high-contrast token pair.
  - Streamed markdown for assistant text.
  - Tool parts: name + status + domain icon, input collapsed by default, compact output.
  - Composer: persistent focus, "Thinking…" indicator during `submitted`.
  - Identity: domain-specific `gemma_brain` glyph, not `Sparkles`.

### 5.3 Conversation/storage

Conversation persistence is handled by the **memory loop** (`mem://features/memory-loop`) backed by **cognitive-mcp** (`100.90.37.254:3003`). No Supabase, no browser localStorage, no XDG JSON files.

- **Memory loop** owns the conversation lifecycle: append, recall, summarization, eviction. Chat transcripts are fed into the loop as `evt.*` records and recalled by semantic search through cognitive-mcp's Qdrant-backed memory tools.
- **cognitive-mcp** is the persistence gateway. The native client never writes chat state to disk directly; it dispatches memory-store actions through the existing gRPC → D-Bus → cognitive-mcp path.
- Conversation shape (threaded vs. single) is still gathered via `questions--ask_questions` before implementation, but storage is settled: memory loop + cognitive-mcp, always.
- If threaded, `thread_id` is a cognitive-mcp memory key, not a database row ID. Native route is `Route::Chat(thread_id)` in `nav.rs`.

### 5.4 Lovable AI disconnection

- Project-level Lovable AI Gateway is disconnected; `LOVABLE_API_KEY` is removed from project secrets.
- Any pre-existing `src/lib/ai-gateway*`, `supabase/functions/chat`, or `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider code is deleted.
- The repo README states explicitly: **all model inference is self-hosted in `gemma_brain`; no external AI gateway is in use.**

## 6. Failure modes

| Failure | Behavior |
|---|---|
| gRPC bootstrap fails | Console renders connection diagnostic surface; retries with backoff. |
| Reflection missing a descriptor | Affected view shows labeled diagnostic; other views unaffected. |
| Chat stream disconnect | Last good transcript preserved; retry with cursor; UI shows reconnecting state. |
| Tool error | Inline tool card flips to error state with compact error payload; transcript continues. |
| `gemma_brain` inference unavailable / overloaded | ChatService returns explicit error frame; UI surfaces actionable status (queue depth, retry hint). |
| Masking violation attempt | Accessor refuses; reasoning-audit records attempt. |

## 7. Security

- **Identity** = caller's WireGuard public key, stored in the identity sled inside the Rust stack (`mem://auth/wireguard-identity`). No JWT, no Supabase auth, no OAuth, no bearer tokens on the wire.
- **Authorization** = RBAC lookup against the identity sled, enforced server-side in `op-web`.
- Chat tools execute server-side only; client cannot invoke arbitrary RPCs through chat.
- Approval-gated tools require explicit operator confirmation in the chat UI.
- All chat tool calls + results recorded in the blockchain audit pipeline (`mem://features/security/audit-and-search`).
- No model traffic ever leaves the operator network — there is no outbound call to a hosted AI gateway.
- **No Supabase at runtime** (`mem://constraints/no-supabase-runtime-use`): no `public` tables, RLS policies, edge functions, or storage buckets are read or written by the application.

## 8. Trade-offs accepted

- **Native-only runtime** vs. browser convenience — accepted; operator workflow demands it.
- **Self-hosted inference** vs. managed AI gateway — accepted; data sovereignty and offline operation outrank managed convenience. We give up the AI SDK ecosystem (`streamText`, provider switching) but keep its `UIMessage` wire vocabulary so renderers stay portable.
- **Two design surfaces (React + egui)** vs. one — accepted as design workspace cost; offset by shared schema/DSL contracts.

**Rules:**
- All inference is local to operator infrastructure (`gemma_brain`). No external model calls.
- Tools are defined in Rust with `schemars` input schemas; each tool wraps an `op-plugins` RPC and runs server-side only.
- Mutating tools require approval; approval round-trips via `ChatService.Approve` before `execute` is called.
- Agent loop bounded at ≥50 steps; cancellable via `ChatService.Cancel`.
- Wire vocabulary mirrors AI SDK `UIMessage` part kinds (`text` / `tool-call` / `tool-result` / `reasoning`) so renderers stay portable — this is a wire-format choice, not a runtime dependency on the AI SDK.
- Structured tool outputs are JSON validated against the tool's declared `schemars` schema before being framed.

## 5. Native chat rendering contract

| AI Elements primitive | egui equivalent |
|---|---|
| `Conversation` + `ConversationContent` + `ConversationScrollButton` | `chat::view::transcript` with sticky-to-bottom |
| `Message` / `MessageContent` / `MessageResponse` | `chat::view::message` (role-styled, markdown-rendered) |

input.new_str:
## 5. Embedded Chat (Antigravity-style)

The chat panel lives **inside** `zeroclaw-gui` as the `Chat` route, the way Antigravity embeds its agent in the IDE shell. It is not a separate window or a browser popup.

**LLM routing authority:** `zeroclaw` owns LLM provider/model routing (OD-28). The `zeroclaw` plugin carries `selected_provider` / `selected_model` and is the single routing authority. The `op-llm` crate's runtime switching (`switch_provider` / `switch_model` via `/api/llm/*`) is removed and consolidated under zeroclaw. `gemma_brain` handles routing-compliance, subid classification, 4-perspectives, and gallery projections; it consumes the `large_language_model` plugin (model-agnostic, model is a swappable field) but does not own provider selection. The chatbot model is interchangeable — gemma is just one model in this model-agnostic stack.

**Hosting:** all inference happens on our own infrastructure. No external AI gateway. **Lovable AI Gateway is not used.** No `LOVABLE_API_KEY`, no `ai.gateway.lovable.dev`, no third-party hosted models.

The actual chatbot model is **interchangeable** — `gemma_brain` routes chat requests to whichever model backend is configured. **Lovable AI Gateway is not used.** No `LOVABLE_API_KEY`, no `ai.gateway.lovable.dev`, no third-party hosted models. The AI SDK provider helper is removed.

input.new_str:
### 5.1 Server side (`op-web` ChatService)

- New gRPC service `ChatService` with:
  - `Send(SendRequest) returns (stream ChatFrame)` — streams `UIMessagePart` events as binary-framed gRPC-Web frames.
- **Routing is zeroclaw's authority.** `SendRequest` carries the provider/model selection from zeroclaw's `selected_provider` / `selected_model` state. `op-web` is the gRPC façade and tool dispatcher; it does not own provider switching. The `op-llm` crate's `switch_provider` / `switch_model` / `/api/llm/*` endpoints are removed.
- `gemma_brain` applies compliance tags and subid classification to chat frames; it does not select the model. It consumes the `large_language_model` plugin for cognitive projections (gallery, reasoning, 4-perspectives).
- Tool catalog defined in Rust (typed argument schemas via `schemars`), each tool wraps an existing `op-plugins` RPC.
- Mutating tools require explicit approval; approval round-trips through the chat panel via `ChatService.Approve`.
- Agent loop is bounded (≥50 steps) and cancellable via `ChatService.Cancel`.
- System prompt, tool catalog, and persona come from `gemma_brain`'s persona registry stream.
- The wire shape mirrors the AI SDK `UIMessage` part vocabulary (text / tool-call / tool-result / reasoning) so renderers stay portable, but the producer is our own runtime — no AI SDK `streamText` / `toUIMessageStreamResponse` call exists on the server.

The egui chat view mirrors AI Elements semantics; it does not invent new primitives.

| AI Elements primitive | egui equivalent |
|---|---|
| `Conversation` + `ConversationContent` + `ConversationScrollButton` | `chat::view::transcript` with sticky-to-bottom |
| `Message` / `MessageContent` / `MessageResponse` | `chat::view::message` (role-styled, markdown-rendered) |
| `Tool` / `ToolHeader` / `ToolInput` / `ToolOutput` | `chat::view::tool_card` (input collapsed by default, including completed/error) |
| `PromptInput` / `PromptInputTextarea` / `PromptInputSubmit` | `chat::view::composer` (always-focused, status-aware submit) |
| `Shimmer` | `chat::view::thinking` ("Thinking…" while `submitted`) |

**Style invariants:**
- Assistant messages: no background bubble; render on the page surface.
- User messages: filled bubble with a deliberate high-contrast token pair from `theme.rs`.
- Identity glyph: domain-specific mark (`gemma_brain`), never `Sparkles`.
- Tool input/output cards stay collapsed by default in all states.

## 6. Conversation & storage contract

Conversation persistence is handled by the **memory loop** (`mem://features/memory-loop`) backed by **cognitive-mcp** (`100.90.37.254:3003`). No Supabase, no browser localStorage, no XDG JSON files.

- **Memory loop** owns the conversation lifecycle: append, recall, summarization, eviction. Chat transcripts are fed into the loop as `evt.*` records and recalled by semantic search through cognitive-mcp's Qdrant-backed memory tools.
- **cognitive-mcp** is the persistence gateway. The native client never writes chat state to disk directly; it dispatches memory-store actions through the existing gRPC → D-Bus → cognitive-mcp path.
- Conversation shape (threaded vs. single) is still gathered via `questions--ask_questions` before implementation, but storage is settled: memory loop + cognitive-mcp, always.
- If threaded → `Route::Chat(thread_id)` in `nav.rs` for native; `thread_id` is a cognitive-mcp memory key, not a database row ID.

# Requirements — Operator Console Topology

**Feature:** Native `zeroclaw-gui` operator console as the sole runtime, with `lovable/` React SPA demoted to a design workspace, and an Antigravity-IDE-style embedded chat agent (AI SDK + Lovable AI Gateway) as the primary operator-to-system interface.

**Status:** Draft
**Owner:** AI Agent (authoritative)
**Related memory:** `mem://tech/architecture`, `mem://tech/communication-protocol`, `mem://tech/grpc-dbus-mirror-architecture`, `mem://tech/grpc-network-routing`, `mem://tech/state-projection-store`, `mem://features/streaming`, `mem://features/grpc-diagnostics`, `mem://features/generative-ui/json-render-catalog`

---

## 1. User stories

### US-1 — Single operator runtime
As an operator, I want one native console (`zeroclaw-gui`) that runs out-of-browser so that I am not subject to browser sandbox limits, tab lifecycle, or JS GC pauses during incident response.

**Acceptance:**
- `zeroclaw-gui` is the only artifact shipped to operator workstations.
- The React SPA is not published as a production surface.
- Vite preview exists for design iteration only and is clearly labeled as such.

### US-2 — React workspace is design-only
As the AI Agent, I want `lovable/` retained as a prototyping sandbox so that views, theme tokens, nav layout, and schema-driven widgets can be iterated quickly before porting to egui.

**Acceptance:**
- `lovable/` contains no production business logic.
- Every component in `lovable/` has a counterpart or design-only marker.
- README at repo root states the two-system split.

### US-3 — gRPC-Web as the only client transport
As the system, I want all client/server traffic over gRPC-Web with binary 5-byte framing so that protocol shape is uniform across native and (legacy) browser clients.

**Acceptance:**
- No REST endpoints in the production path of `op-web`.
- All RPCs are reachable via `ServerReflection`.
- High-frequency streams use the SSE/WS sidecar documented in `mem://features/streaming`.

### US-4 — Schema-as-code contract
As the renderer, I want every payload describable by a `schemars` Schema so that UI rendering is generic and does not require per-message code.

**Acceptance:**
- Every plugin state struct derives `schemars::JsonSchema`.
- `schema.rs` renders any `(Schema, Value)` pair without crashing.
- Unknown schema constructs degrade to a labeled diagnostic frame, never a raw JSON dump outside one.

### US-5 — gemma_brain owns projections
As the system, I want `gemma_brain` to be the projection owner for gallery, reasoning, and persona registry so that the client never recomputes derived state.

**Acceptance:**
- No client-side derivation of gallery or persona state.
- Projections stream through gRPC; `zeroclaw-gui` mirrors into `useEventStore`-equivalent stores.
- D-Bus mirror stays 1:1 with gRPC truth (`mem://tech/grpc-dbus-mirror-architecture`).

### US-6 — Strip SPA-only paths from `op-web`
As the codebase, I want `op-web` free of SPA-only handlers so that the cutover to native-only is real and not a parallel deployment.

**Acceptance:**
- `handlers/gemma.rs`, `handlers/ui_gallery.rs`, `/api/gemma/*`, and rust-embed of Vite `dist/` removed.
- `op-web` binary size drops accordingly.
- CI gate prevents reintroduction of SPA-only routes.

### US-7 — Embedded chat agent (Antigravity-style)
As an operator, I want a chat surface embedded directly into the console — the same way Antigravity puts an agent panel inside the IDE — so that I can converse with `gemma_brain`, invoke tools, watch streamed tool activity, and stay in one window.

**Acceptance:**
- A dedicated `Chat` route in `nav.rs` opens a persistent panel inside `zeroclaw-gui`.
- The chat surface is served entirely by our own server-side AI in `gemma_brain` / `op-web` — **no Lovable AI Gateway, no third-party hosted inference, no `LOVABLE_API_KEY`**.
- Wire format follows the AI SDK `UIMessage` part shape (text, tool-call, tool-result, reasoning) so the renderer stays interchangeable, but the producer is our own model runtime, not the AI SDK provider library.
- Tool activity renders inline with status, collapsible input, and compact output (closed by default).
- The composer stays focused by default; submit disabled while `submitted`/`streaming`.
- Conversation shape and storage are chosen via `questions--ask_questions` per `chat-agent-ui-contract` before implementation.
- Assistant identity uses a domain-specific mark — never the generic `Sparkles` icon.

### US-8 — No hand-rolled chat renderers
As the codebase, I want the chat UI assembled from one set of primitives (AI Elements-shaped in the React workspace, egui-shaped in `zeroclaw-gui`) so that the experience is consistent across surfaces.

**Acceptance:**
- React workspace chat composes `Conversation`, `Message`, `MessageResponse`, `PromptInput`, `Tool*`, `Shimmer` from AI Elements **as renderers only**, pointed at our gRPC `ChatService` — not any Lovable endpoint.
- Native chat in `zeroclaw-gui` consumes the same `UIMessagePart` stream over gRPC-Web framing.
- No bespoke transcript, tool accordion, or composer outside those renderers.

### US-9 — Disconnect Lovable AI features
As the project, I want Lovable AI / AI Gateway features explicitly disabled so that nothing in the codebase implies external model hosting.

**Acceptance:**
- `LOVABLE_API_KEY` is not referenced by any production code path.

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| NFR-1 | Cold-start of `zeroclaw-gui` to first rendered frame < 500ms on operator workstation. |

| NFR-3 | Schema renderer handles ≥10k-node payloads via virtualization without dropping frames. |
| NFR-4 | High-frequency streams update store imperatively (no per-frame React/egui repaint storm). |
| NFR-5 | Chat tokens stream end-to-end with <150ms p50 first-token latency on Lovable AI Gateway. |
| NFR-6 | Masking rules (`mem://features/security-masking`) enforced on every rendered payload, including tool results in chat. |
| NFR-7 | Native binary contains no JS runtime, no Chromium, no webview. |

- Mobile or tablet operator console.
- Multi-operator collaborative editing inside the chat panel.
- A/B routing between models (deferred to a separate spec).

- Should tool approval (`needsApproval`) gate destructive backplane ops by default?
- Does the React workspace ship a publishable chat preview, or is chat native-only?

### US-7 — Embedded Antigravity IDE interface
As an operator, I want the Antigravity IDE interface embedded directly into the console — JSON-rendered through the json-render DSL with the Antigravity SDK baked in — so that I can converse with the system, invoke tools, watch streamed tool activity, and stay in one window.

**Acceptance:**
- A dedicated `Chat` route in `nav.rs` opens a persistent panel inside `zeroclaw-gui`.
- The chat surface is the actual Antigravity IDE interface, not a reimplementation. It is JSON-rendered via the json-render DSL interpreter (`generative-ui-catalog` spec) with the Antigravity SDK baked in.
- The chatbot model is interchangeable; `gemma_brain` routes and applies compliance tags but is not the model itself.
- **No Lovable AI Gateway, no third-party hosted inference, no `LOVABLE_API_KEY`.**
- Wire format follows the AI SDK `UIMessage` part shape (text, tool-call, tool-result, reasoning) so the renderer stays interchangeable, but the producer is our own runtime, not the AI SDK provider library.
- Tool activity renders inline with status, collapsible input, and compact output (closed by default).
- The composer stays focused by default; submit disabled while `submitted`/`streaming`.
- Conversation shape (threaded vs. single) is chosen via `questions--ask_questions` before implementation. Storage is settled: memory loop + cognitive-mcp (see US-11).
- Assistant identity uses a domain-specific operator console mark — never `Sparkles`, never tied to a specific model.

### US-8 — No hand-rolled chat renderers
As the codebase, I want the chat UI assembled from the Antigravity SDK components rendered through the json-render DSL interpreter so that the experience is consistent and no bespoke primitives exist.

**Acceptance:**
- Native chat in `zeroclaw-gui` maps Antigravity SDK components (`Conversation`, `Message`, `MessageResponse`, `PromptInput`, `Tool*`, `Shimmer`) through the DSL interpreter to egui primitives.
- No bespoke transcript, tool accordion, or composer outside the DSL interpreter.
- No React workspace chat mirror exists. Chat is native-only.
